statement.text:
A semigroup presentation is called tree-like if all relations have the form a = bc
where a, b, c are letters and no two relations share the left-hand side or the right-hand
side. Is it decidable whether the semigroup given by a finite tree-like presentation
contains an idempotent?
    This is equivalent to the question whether the closure of a finitely generated sub-
group of R. Thompson’s group F contains an isomorphic copy of F .                 M. Sapir
